hero.alt: Warm sand coloured illustration with the title Does Vaping Break Wudu

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 225, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Prayer of one who has broken wudu is not accepted until he performs ablution.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 176, Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Abu Hurairah explains hadath as the passing of wind.

sources.title: Does smoking invalidate ablution, Egypt's Dar al-Ifta
sources.supports: Smoking does not invalidate ablution; cleanse the mouth of the odour before prayer.

sources.title: Smoking break wudhu, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: Smoking does not break wudu; preferable to clean the mouth before prayer or recitation.

sources.title: Vaping During Ihraam, Darul Ifta Birmingham
sources.supports: Vaping is similar to smoking, deemed haram or at least makruh tahrimi; not an ihram prohibition.

sources.title: Hukum menggunakan vape, MUIS
sources.supports: Fatwa Committee rules all vapes and Kpod haram based on harm and protection of life and mind.

review.notes: Read each retrieved page this run: Dar al-Ifta and Darul Ifta Birmingham smoking fatwas, Birmingham vaping fatwa (ihram context), MUIS Malay fatwa (summary paragraph read and translated), and hadith Muslim 225 and Bukhari 176. No source addresses vaping and wudu directly, so the article labels that as an inference from the smoking rulings. Ruling on permissibility is kept separate from wudu validity.
